hunt.justification: Medicare-themed social engineering causes high financial and identity risk to employees, which can bleed into corporate credential reuse; a negative result confirms robust user hygiene during peak scam season.

meta.name: Medicare Open Enrollment Social Engineering

related.reason: Generic lookalike hunts are broader but lack the seasonal context and specific impact assessment for healthcare-related fraud.

meta.analysis: A single detection rule on Medicare keywords produces high false positives from legitimate government site usage. This hunt correlates DNS leads with rare HTTP POST behavior and downstream portal sign-ins, allowing an agent to weigh the entire attack chain.

stages.name: Social engineering via malvertising and phishing
observables: Google ads for Medicare plan comparisons or card updates
unsolicited emails or SMS mentioning the December 7 deadline
lookalike domains for medicare.gov or healthcare.gov lacking the .gov suffix

stages.name: Personal and medical data harvesting
observables: HTTP POST requests to lookalike domains containing Medicare numbers or SSNs
accessing or updating onepassword_item_medical_record fields such as medication, dosage, or patient info in response to lures
entry of bank details, credit card information, or account passwords into non-official web forms

stages.name: Fraudulent monetization and account abuse
observables: unauthorized sign-ins to health or banking portals using stolen credentials
manipulation of Medicare enrollment records for fraudulent commissions
suspicious Medicare claims for services or prescriptions never received

scenario.summary: A seasonal social engineering campaign during the Medicare Open Enrollment period (Oct 15 - Dec 7) uses Google ads, phishing emails, and SMS to direct victims to fraudulent lookalike websites. These sites are used to harvest Medicare numbers, Social Security numbers, and account credentials to facilitate identity theft, healthcare fraud, and fraudulent enrollment manipulation.

meta.rationale: Focus on general user workstation segments. This hunt is highly seasonal and should be run periodically during the Medicare Open Enrollment period (Oct 15 - Dec 7).
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using lookalike domains during the Medicare Open Enrollment season to harvest personal and medical data via social engineering, subsequently using those credentials to access sensitive health and banking portals.

hunt.name: Medicare Open Enrollment Social Engineering
hunt.description: This hunt identifies seasonal social engineering campaigns targeting Medicare beneficiaries. It uses a gated flow: first, a low-cost DNS scoping step identifies hosts interacting with non-government domains containing Medicare keywords. If an agent confirms these as suspicious lures, the hunt performs an expensive parallel fan-out to analyze HTTP POST data-harvesting patterns and concurrent unauthorized sign-ins to sensitive portals. This approach isolates the transition from the initial lure to the monetization of stolen identity and health data.

nodes.label: Lead DNS lookups for Medicare lures

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, query_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%medicare%' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%healthcare%') AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.gov' AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.gov.%' AND instr(',' || '{{legit_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') = 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify potential social engineering lures by finding DNS queries for domains containing Medicare keywords that do not end in official .gov TLDs.
config.expected_signal: DNS queries for Medicare-themed domains on non-government infrastructure. Silence suggests no users have visited obvious lures in the window.

config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict on whether the DNS activity suggests a user was targeted by a seasonal scam.

nodes.label: Rare HTTP POST targets for Medicare keywords

config.content: SELECT url_hostname, url_path, actor_user_name, device_hostname, COUNT(*) AS request_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_http_activity WHERE http_method = 'POST' AND (LOWER(url_hostname) LIKE '%medicare%' OR LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%medicare%' OR LOWER(url_hostname) LIKE '%healthcare%' OR LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%healthcare%') AND LOWER(url_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.gov' AND LOWER(url_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.gov.%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY url_hostname, url_path, actor_user_name, device_hostname HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 3 ORDER BY first_seen DESC
config.description: Detect potential harvesting behavior by finding rare domains receiving POST requests containing Medicare keywords, filtered to the scoped hosts.
config.expected_signal: POST requests to rare, non-government domains containing Medicare keywords. This identifies the data-submission stage of the phishing attack.

config.description: Identify potential credential abuse by finding sign-in activity to sensitive portals from the same scoped hosts.
